memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So I will stretch out my hand and strike the Egyptians with all the wonders that I will perform among them. After that, he will let you go." - Exodus 3:20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice who does the work in this verse. I will stretch out my hand. I will strike. I will perform.

Moses will carry the staff and speak the words, but no one will be able to mistake whose power delivered Israel. God had already made sure of that by choosing an eighty-year-old shepherd with a speech problem instead of a general with an army.

This is a pattern throughout Scripture. God deliberately works through weak instruments so that the glory is unmistakably His. Paul understood it well — we carry this treasure in clay jars, so that the surpassing power is seen to be from God and not from us (2 Cor 4:7).

If you have ever felt too small for what God has asked, remember that your smallness is not a problem for God. It may be the point.

Do the part God gives you. Speak, serve, go, pray. But do not carry a weight that was never yours. The outcome rests on His hand, not yours.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I trying to produce results that only God can produce?
2. Where do I need to hand an outcome back to God today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Almighty God, I will do my part faithfully, but the outcome is Yours. Stretch out Your hand where I am powerless. Amen.
